claims.text: Increasing lattice distortion and local chemical ordering in refractory HEAs will enhance high-temperature mechanical strength.
Increasing lattice distortion and local chemical ordering will alter the thermoelastic response of refractory HEAs.
Final heat-treatment variations can adjust lattice distortion and nanoscale chemical ordering without changing overall composition or bulk structure.
Processing-induced lattice distortion and local chemical ordering alter dislocation mobility.
Processing-induced lattice distortion and local chemical ordering alter atomic bonding environments.
Increased lattice distortion and local ordering modify the energy barriers for dislocation motion.
Modified barriers to dislocation motion enhance high-temperature strength.
Changes in atomic-scale bonding caused by distortion and ordering alter thermoelastic behavior.
Rapid quenching will produce greater lattice distortion and local chemical ordering than controlled annealing.
The rapidly quenched variant will have measurably higher high-temperature strength than the annealed baseline.
The rapidly quenched variant will exhibit a distinct shift in thermoelastic parameters relative to the annealed baseline.
The rapidly quenched variant may exhibit a lower thermal expansion coefficient than the annealed baseline.
The proposed effects are limited to 800–1200°C under controlled mechanical loading.
Nanoprecipitate formation may confound the relationship between heat treatment, lattice distortion or ordering, and measured properties.
